solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Yank grabbing Conservative fellow's mistress?

indicators.note: the word for yank takes hold of the following letters, so they sit inside it

parts.note: to yank something is to tear or pull it violently
a fellow is a man, he

explanation.surface: An American seizing a Tory man's lover, with a question about who she is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American but is a verb meaning pull. 'mistress' is a schoolmistress, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmistress is a woman who instructs pupils, so the word can stand for a classroom educator.

clue.text: Prime minister cutting Her Majesty's hair

indicators.note: cutting says the royal letters are removed from the prime minister's name

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher, British PM 1979-90
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A prime minister trims the Queen's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick mop of hair on someone's head is jokingly compared to a straw roof.

clue.text: Martha occasionally accompanying American in pub, if necessary

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only every other letter of the name
in puts the American letters inside the pub's

parts.note: PH, public house, as on maps
US, United States

explanation.surface: Martha sometimes goes with an American to the pub, if needs be.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means only with effort or under pressure, so when it is absolutely required.

clue.text: Boss tells a whopper about son's latest pieces of news

parts.note: a head is a boss or chief

indicators.note: the words for telling a whopper go around the next letter

parts.note: a whopper is a big lie, so telling one is lying

indicators.note: latest picks the last letter of son

explanation.surface: A boss lies about his son's most recent news.
explanation.definitionFit: Headlines are the main news stories, the top items in a bulletin.

clue.text: Reminisced about Bolshevik holding English rally

indicators.note: the word for Bolshevik holds the following letters inside

parts.note: a red is a communist
to rally is to collect or gather together

explanation.surface: Reminiscing about a communist who held an English demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: Recalling memories of something is recollecting it; the transitive verb takes an object, matching 'about'.

clue.text: Group of shadowy figures holding church back

indicators.note: the shadowy figures hold the next letters within them

parts.note: spies are figures operating in the shadows

indicators.note: back says the letters for church are read in reverse

parts.note: CE, the Church of England

explanation.surface: A band of mysterious figures keeping a church at bay.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a species is a classification grouping of similar organisms.

clue.text: Brussels upset after Brexiters' final charge

indicators.note: after puts the reversed Brussels letters behind the final letter of Brexiters
final takes the last letter of Brexiters
upset, in a down clue, turns the letters upside down so they read backwards

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU, European Union

explanation.surface: Brussels is annoyed at the Brexiters' last accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone in a court of law is to bring a suit, to prosecute.

clue.text: Stops head resigning and relaxes

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the word for stops quits

parts.note: ceases means stops or ends

explanation.surface: The head teacher quits and everyone calms down.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to loosen or make less tense, the same as to relax.

clue.text: In speech I nag, unfeeling

indicators.note: in speech says the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: I nag is 'I scold'

explanation.surface: Someone admits that when they talk they nag, without emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unfeeling is coldly unemotional, with no warmth at all.

clue.text: Career crazily with son, guzzling new wine

indicators.note: guzzling means swallowing, so the scrambled letters take in the next one
crazily means the letters of career are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone runs wildly with their son while gulping wine.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a white wine from the Loire valley in France.

clue.text: A snowdrop?

parts.note: read not as the flower but as a drop, or fall, of snow down a mountainside

explanation.surface: A little white spring flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge mass of snow sliding down a mountain is literally snow dropping.

clue.text: Geese flying east into cover

indicators.note: the letter for east goes into the word for cover

parts.note: skin is the covering of a body
E is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: Geese heading eastwards towards shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A flock of wild geese in flight is called by this collective noun.

clue.text: Peasant's husband seized by large force one heading west

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: the husband's letter is held inside the letters that follow
the large force taken as one unit runs leftwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: L is the clothing abbreviation for large
RUC, the Royal Ulster Constabulary, a police force

explanation.surface: A peasant's husband is arrested by a large police unit heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: L + RUC reversed gives CURL, with H inside. The RUC was Northern Ireland's police force until 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: A churl is an archaic word for a rustic of low rank, a serf or countryman.

clue.text: Loot needs shifting: all eyes are on it

definitions.note: something that draws attention to itself, a centre of attraction

indicators.note: the letters of loot needs are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Stolen goods have to be moved while everybody is watching.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetic rock attracts iron, and figuratively anything that attracts attention is one.

clue.text: Tousled beauty had fun going topless

parts.note: a dish is an attractive person

indicators.note: the word for had fun loses its top, or first letter, in a down clue

parts.note: revelled means partied, had fun

explanation.surface: A messy-haired beauty enjoyed herself by going topless.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair that is tousled is untidy and rumpled, with a dishevelled look.

clue.text: Feeble toff somehow led Cornish news

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of led Cornish news are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A weak aristocrat somehow led the news in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a British idiom for an ineffectual upper-class man, pictured with a receding jaw.

clue.text: Independently working on European broadcast

parts.note: on, as in the machine is on, working
broadcast seed is scattered, or sown

explanation.surface: Independently working on a European broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio or TV, but its old sense is scattering seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something alone, without help from anyone, is doing it independently.

clue.text: Founder lacking sparkle after trip

indicators.note: after places the word for lacking sparkle behind the trip

parts.note: a trip is a stumble or fall
flat, as of a drink gone without fizz

explanation.surface: A company's founder lacks pizzazz after a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Founder' looks like a noun, a company's creator, but it is the verb meaning fail.
explanation.definitionFit: To founder is to fail or collapse, like a plan or joke that falls short.

clue.text: How one might face grandmaster or general?

definitions.meaning: a chess opponent sits facing a grandmaster on the far side of the chessboard
applying to everyone or everything, all-inclusive

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means applying universally; literally it describes a chess player's position opposite their rival.

clue.text: Continuation of American's truly gripping novel

indicators.note: the American word holds the next letters

parts.note: in American speech 'real' means truly or very, as in 'real good'
novel means new

explanation.surface: A sequel to an American's genuinely gripping novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Renewing a contract or lease extends it, so a renewal is a continuation.

clue.text: Some reactionary tweets I'm deranged, anger clouding judgement

indicators.note: reactionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A right-wing tweeter admits to being unhinged, so furious they cannot think straight.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a fit of fury so strong it blinds one to reason.

clue.text: Unaffectionate father I like to send up

parts.note: FR, Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: send up in a down clue sends the letters upward, reversing them

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it

explanation.surface: Someone cold to their father, whom they like to mock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'send up' looks like mocking; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid means cold in manner, lacking warmth or affection.

clue.text: One crying out from back of court

definitions.text: One crying out from back of court

parts.words: One crying out from back of court
parts.note: a tennis official at the baseline calls 'Out!' when a ball lands beyond it

explanation.surface: Someone yelling from the rear of a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crying out' suggests shouting in distress, and 'court' a law court; it is a tennis court and the call 'Out!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis official stationed along a court boundary calls balls landing outside it.

clue.text: Do wrong in Jersey on vacation, procuring pot

indicators.note: in places the word for doing wrong inside the outer letters
vacated, Jersey is emptied of its inner letters

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Getting into trouble on holiday in Jersey by buying cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' suggests cannabis but is a chamber pot. Jersey is one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerry is old British slang for a chamber pot kept under the bed.

clue.text: Senior man joining up after wife departs

indicators.note: departs says the letter for wife leaves the word

parts.note: a welder is a worker who joins metal parts

explanation.surface: An older man enlists once his wife has left him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining up' suggests enlisting, but it is joining metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a senior person, older or higher in rank.

clue.text: Put down a cow?

definitions.meaning: to set down or bring something down
a cow lows, or moos, so it is something that lows

explanation.definitionFit: Lowering means setting something down, and a mooing animal is jokingly one that lows.

clue.text: Striking, moving fast after change of leader

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for moving fast is swapped for another

parts.note: galloping is moving at speed, like a horse

explanation.surface: Hitting while rushing along after a new head took over.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallop is a heavy blow, so striking hard is this; it also means huge.

clue.text: Try to win women's love on more than one occasion

parts.note: W for women

indicators.note: the score of love is given twice over

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Trying again and again to win a woman's affections.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to seek their affection or favour.

clue.text: House on square? Let's get it!

indicators.note: on, in a down-or-across charade, puts the house after the square

parts.note: to square with is to tally, agree

explanation.surface: A building on a town square, with an eager cry to grab it.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts the house second. The answer is the cry fox hunters give on sighting the fox.
explanation.definitionFit: Huntsmen shout this when the fox is spotted, urging the pack to go after the quarry.

clue.text: Saw nurses at work — so gifted!

indicators.note: nurses means holds tenderly, so the word for saw contains the next letters

parts.note: to see someone romantically is to have dated them
on, as in on duty

explanation.surface: Seeing nurses on duty, someone exclaims how talented they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a tool or a past tense of see; it is past tense in the romantic sense. 'gifted' looks like talented but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifted as a verb means handed over freely, synonymous with gave away to a cause.
